progesterone did not protect against the testicular toxicity of cadmium in rats, but increased the toxicity of cadmium to Fischer (F344), but not Wistar (WF), rats.
progesterone did not reduce the testicular toxicity of cadmium in either Fischer 344 or Wistar rats.
progesterone did not protect against cadmium-induced testis toxicity in male Fischer or Wistar rats.

the effects of cadmium (Cd), a heavy metal, on male fertility and reproduction.
the effect of cadmium (CdCl2) on testicular structure and function in the Fischer 344 (F344) rat and the role of metallothionein in Cd-induced testicular damage.
the mechanisms of cadmium-induced male reproductive toxicity.

progesterone can increase the lethality of CdCl2 in mice, rats, and rabbits.

progesterone is not a general protective agent against cadmium-induced toxicity in rats.
